To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
overexpression of ALK1 in ECs prevents development of AVM in mouse models of hereditary hemorrhagic telengiectasia.

overexpression of Activin receptor-like kinase 1 (ALK1) in endothelial cells (EO) suppresses development of arteriovenous malformations in mouse models of Hereditary hemorrhagic Telangiectasias (HHT).

(1) Overexpression of the ALk1 receptor in endothelial cells suppresses development of AVM in mouse models of HHT; (2) ALK1-over-expression can be a promising therapy for HHT1; (3) ALK1 over-expression can be a safe therapy for HHT2; (4) ENG-over-expression cannot suppress AVMs in mouse models of Alk1-iKOs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of TGF- β signaling pathway in the development of Aneurysm.
the role of the endothelial-specific receptor ALK1 and its ligand BMP9 in the formation of a normal vasculature.
the development of novel therapeutic strategies for the treatment of HHT1, HHT2, and HHT3, which have been shown to be caused by mutations in the ENG, ALK-1, and SMAD4 genes, respectively.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ALK1-OEs in HHT1 and -2 patients could prevent AVM formation and improve their quality of life.
overexpression of ALK1 in ECs suppresses the development of A/V malformations in HHT1 and 2 mice models.
ALK1-OEs are a promising therapeutic approach for HHT1 or HHT2.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ALK1 is a key molecule for the angiogenic response of ECs and that the ALK1-SMAD pathway is a promising therapeutic target for the treatment of HHT.
we have shown that ALK1-OEs can be an effective therapy for HHT1 or HHT2 in mouse models, but we could not demonstrate that ENG-OEs can be effective for HHT1 in mouse models.
ALK1-OEs in endothelial cells can be used for treatment of HHT1 and 2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
overexpression of ALK1 in endothelial cells can suppress development of AVM in mouse models of HHT.
overexpressing ALK1 in endothelial cells of mice that are genetically deficient in ALK1 or ENG prevents the development of arteriovenous malformation.
ALK1 is the main receptor of the ALK-1/Eng-Smad4 signaling pathway, which is essential for the formation of the proper arteriovenosus network.
